heading: Sigil-Making
paragraphs: A sigil is a desire reduced to a single mark — a phrase of intent folded into a symbol, then set alight and released. The technique is attributed to the artist-occultist Austin Osman Spare, who taught that a wish, distilled past the reach of doubt, works on the mind the way a seed works on the soil: quietly, and in its own season.
As with everything in this book: respect the craft, honor the spirits, and let your intentions be pure. Do not make sigils aimed at another's will.
A quiet hour, a sheet of paper, a pen consecrated (or simply reserved) for this work, and a fireproof bowl or a patch of earth where you have leave to bury paper.
1. Write your intent as though it is already true

Write one sentence stating what you seek, in the present tense, as if it has already come to pass. "I am a homeowner" serves better than "I want a house." Keep it short, keep it specific, and keep it positive — phrase toward what you desire, never away from what you fear. A sentence that makes you exhale with relief is ready; one that makes you flinch is not.
Remember the second half of every working: the sigil plants the intention, but the walking remains yours. Do not ask the craft to do what you will not.
2. Strip the sentence to its letters

Cross out every vowel, then every letter that repeats itself, until only a skeleton of unique consonants remains. From "I AM CREATIVE," for example, you might keep M C R T V. These are your raw materials.

Draw the letters into one another — interlock them, stack them, turn them sideways — until the sentence is unrecognizable and a single glyph stands in its place. Simple is strong; intricate is permitted. Work it until it pleases your eye. When you can no longer read the wish in it, the wish has gone where it needs to go.
4. Charge it and let it go

Choose your element. By fire: in a calm and grounded state, hold the sigil, repeat your intent, and burn it in the fireproof bowl — seeing, in your mind's eye, the outcome already unfolding — then imagine the rising heat carrying the charge out into the world. Never leave a burning object unattended. By earth: bury the folded sigil with thanks, and walk away without looking back. Either way, the final act is release. A watched seed is never a planted one.

- A candle of a color that matches your intent (green for growth, gold for prosperity, white for clarity) - Incense or herb smoke that suits the aim - The moon's phase: waxing to draw toward you, waning to release
Sign and date the entry when you begin; when the working ripens, note it in the margin — for the next keeper, who will learn from your hand as you learned from theirs.
